Document: MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT

Findings:
[{"id":"f-ip-400d3fcd","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 14.1 As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services. No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.","rationale":"The IP package meets our preferred position. § 14.1 confirms Customer owns all Customer Data, Confidential Information and independently developed IP, with no transfer to Vendor beyond a processing right limited to delivering the Services. § 14.2 vests ownership of Deliverables in Customer with an express present assignment from Vendor plus personnel assignments and further-assurances. § 14.3 leaves Vendor with only its pre-existing Vendor Technology and routes embedded Vendor Technology to the § 13.2 perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, modify and create derivative works for Customer's business (including Affiliates and contractors). § 14.4 expressly negates joint ownership absent a signed instrument and keeps feedback voluntary with Customer retaining unrestricted use. § 15.1 further bars model training on Customer Data without our consent. Minor points noted but not deviations: Deliverable ownership is tied to payment of Fees and to work identified in an Order Form, and the Customer Data definition carves out anonymized operational telemetry that cannot be linked back to us — neither assigns our IP or data to Vendor.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-c4f0f7cf","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.","rationale":"Section 24 meets our preferred position in full: § 24.1 lets us assign to an Affiliate or M&A successor without Vendor consent (notice only); § 24.2 bars Vendor assignment, delegation of material performance or transfer by change of control without our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and never to a direct competitor; § 24.3 applies a reasonable consent standard to other assignments; and § 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees or reduce service on our change of control. § 13.3 aligns licence transfer with a Section 24 permitted assignment, and no other provision (including the § 9.2 insolvency clause) creates a Vendor exit or re-pricing right on our change of control. No redline needed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-fafccb43","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor. Customer owes Fees only for conforming Services provided through the effective termination date, and Vendor shall promptly refund prepaid Fees allocable to the period after that date. Vendor has no corresponding convenience-termination right during a committed term.","rationale":"The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, or early-termination/minimum fee payable by us. Searches for \"liquidated damages\", \"penalty\", \"termination fee\", acceleration and minimum-use charges return nothing adverse: Section 9.4 lets us terminate for convenience paying only for conforming Services rendered (with refund of prepaid Fees), Section 7.1 bars unidentified minimum-use charges, Section 27.3 permits termination \"without penalty\", and Section 24.4 bars acceleration of Fees on our change of control. This meets the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages). The Section 2.1 take-or-pay commitment creates economic exposure but is not framed as liquidated damages or a penalty and is addressed under the minimum-commitment rule, so we do not double-flag it here. No redline required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-t4c-572bf3ca","ruleId":"T4C","ruleTitle":"Termination for convenience","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor. Customer owes Fees only for conforming Services provided through the effective termination date, and Vendor shall promptly refund prepaid Fees allocable to the period after that date. Vendor has no corresponding convenience-termination right during a committed term.","rationale":"§ 9.4 meets the preferred position in full: we may terminate the Agreement or any Order Form for convenience (including in part) on thirty days' written notice, with no early-termination fee, we owe Fees only through the effective date, and Vendor must refund prepaid Fees allocable to the post-termination period. It also expressly denies Vendor any corresponding convenience-termination right during a committed term, and a document-wide search for \"for convenience\"/\"terminate\" confirms no Vendor convenience or at-will exit right appears elsewhere (§§ 9.1-9.3 are mutual breach/insolvency and Customer-favourable cause rights; § 24.4 bars Vendor termination on our change of control). No redline is warranted — the clause benefits our party.\n\nNoted but not flagged here: § 2.1's three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay purports to apply \"without reduction or termination rights,\" which is in tension with § 9.4 and could be read to blunt the refund/exit economics. That is a minimum-commitment term addressed under the MINCOMMIT rule, and we should not double-count the same commercial point under T4C; the order-of-precedence provision in § 2.2 does not resolve it, so the conflict is worth a drafting comment when MINCOMMIT is negotiated.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-audit-a71ed49f","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. An audit will be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.","rationale":"§ 22 is the only usage audit/verification right binding us; a document-wide search for audit, inspection, monitoring, verification, remote access and telemetry language surfaced nothing else that could expand it. The clause meets the preferred position on every material term: frequency is capped at once in any twelve-month period, notice is thirty days' prior written notice, audits are limited to normal business hours and to licence-quantity compliance, and they must be off-site where practicable and conducted by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality. § 22.2 puts audit costs on Vendor unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent (the preferred 5% trigger, not the 10% fallback), and it expressly bars Vendor and its auditor from accessing Customer systems directly, Customer Data unrelated to usage, privileged material, or another supplier's confidential information — so the walk-away risks of unlimited/unannounced audits and remote system access are excluded. § 22.3 adds customer-favourable protections (findings are our Confidential Information, use limited to enforcing the Agreement, copy of the final report, and payment of a shortfall resolves the audited quantity issue absent fraud or demonstrable error). No redline required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-7f10df38","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 28.1 This Agreement and each dispute arising from it are governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-law principles. The United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods does not apply.","rationale":"Section 28.1 applies New York law and Section 28.2 gives exclusive jurisdiction to the state and federal courts in New York County, with mutual submission to personal jurisdiction and waiver of venue objections — exactly the playbook preferred position. No arbitration provision appears anywhere in the document (search for \"arbitration\" returned nothing), so there is no foreign seat concern. The Section 28.3 pre-suit executive escalation is a fifteen-business-day meet-and-confer that expressly does not delay urgent relief or limitations-period filings, and the carve-out in 28.2 permitting temporary injunctive relief elsewhere for confidential information or IP is mutual; neither affects the accepted law or forum. Compliant at the preferred position; no redline.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-indemn-af20a8b9","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 20 INDEMNIFICATION 20.1 Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services.","rationale":"Section 20 contains only a one-way, unlimited Customer indemnity of Vendor for \"every claim\" relating to our use of the Services; no Vendor indemnity exists anywhere in the Agreement (searches for \"indemnif\"/\"infring\" return only Sections 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5, which merely reference indemnities). This is walk-away territory under the rule: no Vendor IP indemnity at all plus a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services, so it fails both the preferred and fallback positions. Section 9.3 also relies on remedies \"required by Section 20.5\", which does not exist. We therefore inserted the preferred Vendor indemnity (IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data incidents, gross negligence/wilful misconduct), narrowed our indemnity to Customer-provided content and our breach of law, and added standard notice/control/cooperation procedure, customary IP exclusions and the missing 20.5 procure/modify/replace/refund remedies.","proposal":"Narrow Customer's indemnity to Customer-provided content and breach of law, and add Vendor's IP/misconduct indemnity with notice, control, and cooperation","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-license-6b57f2c0","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 13.1 Vendor grants Customer alone a non-transferable licence, revocable at Vendor's sole discretion, to use the Services without Affiliates or contractors.","rationale":"The Services licence in § 13.1 fails the fallback: it names Customer alone, expressly excludes Affiliates and contractors with no path to add them, is non-transferable, and is revocable at Vendor's sole discretion — which is walk-away territory under this rule. The counterweights only partly help: § 13.2's perpetual, irrevocable licence covering Affiliates and contractors is limited to paid-up software and embedded Deliverables, and § 13.3 (transfer to an Affiliate or successor; revocation only for material uncured breach after notice and cure) contradicts § 13.1's at-will revocation rather than curing the Affiliate/contractor exclusion for the Services. Our redline conforms § 13.1 to the preferred position by extending use to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, tying revocation to the § 13.3 notice-and-cure standard, and adding successor transfer via the § 24 assignment right.","proposal":"Extend the Services licence to Affiliates and contractors and remove revocation at Vendor's discretion","verification":"fail"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-cb7a2001","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 21.1 Each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed Fees actually paid in the one month preceding the event, without exception.","rationale":"The cap is mutual, but at one month of Fees \"actually paid\" it is far below the fallback of twelve months' fees and within walk-away territory (cap below six months' fees). The words \"without exception\" also override the Excluded Claims regime in Section 21.3, placing indemnities, confidentiality, data-protection/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement inside a one-month cap with no super-cap — a second walk-away trigger. Section 21.2 (consequential damages), 21.3 (Excluded Claims definition and payment-obligation carve-out) and 21.4 (independence/severability) are otherwise consistent with the preferred position, so the minimal fix is to restate 21.1 as the greater of twelve months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000 and delete \"without exception\" so the existing carve-outs operate.","proposal":"Cap set at greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000, Excluded Claims uncapped, and payment obligations excluded from damages","verification":"fail"},{"id":"f-mfn-e6e5a72a","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.","rationale":"No MFN or most-favoured-customer obligation runs against Customer anywhere in the agreement: searches for \"most favoured/favourable/favorable\", \"MFN\", \"no less favo\", \"best pricing\", \"benchmark\" and third-party-offer matching return nothing burdening us. § 12.3 affirmatively confirms Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment and preserves our freedom to deal with other suppliers, which meets the preferred position (no MFN obligation on Customer). Nothing to redline; the absence of a Vendor-granted MFN in our favour is a commercial nice-to-have, not a playbook deviation.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-nosolicit-9ac0f612","ruleId":"NOSOLICIT","ruleTitle":"Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.","rationale":"Searches for \"solicit\", \"induce\", \"hire\", \"employ\" and \"recruit\" return no covenant restricting either Party from soliciting or hiring the other's personnel. To the contrary, § 12.3 expressly preserves our freedom to hire anyone responding to general recruitment and records that we have given no no-hire commitment. This matches the playbook preferred position (no non-solicit binding Customer), so no redline is needed; the clause benefits our party.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-renewal-33e30b33","ruleId":"RENEWAL","ruleTitle":"Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.","rationale":"§ 8.2 provides automatic twelve-month (not multi-year) renewals with a Customer opt-out on only thirty days' written notice, plus a Vendor reminder at least sixty days before renewal — and a Customer-favourable extension of the opt-out deadline if the reminder is not sent. § 8.3 caps renewal uplift at the lesser of CPI and three percent, with ninety days' notice of any increase and no increase on prepaid periods. This satisfies the preferred position on renewal term, notice window (30 days ≤ 30) and price cap; no redline needed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-transition-3e7ce3f7","ruleId":"TRANSITION","ruleTitle":"Post-termination transition assistance and data return","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 11.1 Immediately on termination Vendor shall discontinue all assistance and permanently delete Customer Data without offering an export or migration support.","rationale":"Sections 11.2 and 11.3 already deliver the data-return and certified-deletion limbs of the preferred position (return within 30 days of request in a commonly used, machine-readable format; certified deletion only after Customer confirms successful return). However, Section 11.1 sits squarely in walk-away territory: it requires immediate cessation of all assistance and permanent deletion of Customer Data on termination with no export or migration support, and it directly contradicts 11.2/11.3. There is no transition-assistance period anywhere in the agreement, so the clause fails even the 90-day fallback. We replaced 11.1 with up to six months of transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates and subordinated deletion to Sections 11.2 and 11.3, resolving the internal inconsistency with the smallest possible edit; 90 days remains an acceptable fallback.","proposal":"Replace immediate-deletion clause with 6-month transition assistance and align deletion with 11.2/11.3.","verification":"fail"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-75577550","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"low","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 2.2 Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.","rationale":"Section 2.2 binds us to Vendor as sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics for the entire three-year term, with no category limit, no 12-month cap, and no exit on Vendor's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates. That is exclusive dealing for the full term without a performance-based exit — walk-away territory, and it fails the fallback. Section 12.3's acknowledgement that we have made no exclusivity commitment does not cure the problem: it conflicts with the express grant in Section 2.2 and the order-of-precedence clause (the second Section 2.2) does not resolve an internal conflict within the Agreement. We therefore convert the appointment to non-exclusive, reaching the preferred position and aligning Section 2.2 with Section 12.3. We also note the duplicate \"2.2\" numbering, which should be renumbered.","proposal":"Convert Vendor's appointment to non-exclusive, removing the sole-supplier obligation on Customer.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-insurance-32e72a01","ruleId":"INSURANCE","ruleTitle":"Vendor insurance","severity":"low","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 18.1 Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense throughout the term and for one year afterward, commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, employer's liability of USD 1,000,000, professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000.","rationale":"§ 18 contains a full vendor insurance clause that meets the preferred position on every material term: CGL at USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate, professional E&O at USD 2M, cyber and privacy liability at USD 5M, and workers' compensation as required by law, each maintained at Vendor's expense for the term plus one year. § 18.2 adds certificates of insurance and evidence of coverage on request, reputable insurers, primary cover, notice of cancellation, and confirms that insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities. Employer's liability of USD 1M is additional cover beyond the playbook ask and benefits us. No redline required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mincommit-953097f3","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"low","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.","rationale":"§ 2.1 imposes a multi-year (three-year) USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay commitment on us expressly \"without reduction or termination rights\" — squarely the rule's walk-away position, and well short of the fallback (single 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up not penalty). It also conflicts with § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no minimum-volume commitment, and with our § 9.4 convenience-termination right. Redline restores the preferred position: fees for Services used or ordered only, with no minimum, take-or-pay, or shortfall obligation; the fallback commitment structure is offered in the comment.","proposal":"Change § 2.1 to no minimum amount and payment only for Services ordered or used","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-noncompete-768576ee","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"low","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.","rationale":"§ 12.4 binds us (Customer) with a non-compete that survives 24 months post-term, covers any competing product or service, and applies in any territory, with no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions (indeed it expressly bars acquisitions). {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Playbook review of Vendor's Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the MSA against 19 playbook rules. Eleven clauses are compliant, several of them at the preferred position and clearly in our favour: Customer ownership of Customer Data and Deliverables (§ 14), assignment and change-of-control freedom (§ 24), termination for convenience with refund of prepaid Fees (§ 9.4), a tightly bounded once-yearly audit right with a 5% cost-shift trigger (§ 22), New York law and New York County courts (§ 28), 12-month auto-renewal with a 30-day opt-out and a CPI/3% uplift cap (§ 8), full Vendor insurance including USD 5M cyber (§ 18), and no MFN, no-hire or Customer-payable liquidated damages anywhere in the document.

Eight clauses are deviations, and seven of those fall into walk-away territory. The commercial core of the problem is a cluster of Vendor-favourable terms that are internally inconsistent with the rest of the agreement: a three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay with no reduction or termination rights (§ 2.1), sole-source exclusivity for the full term (§ 2.2), a 24-month post-term non-compete on us (§ 12.4), a Services licence that excludes our Affiliates and contractors and is revocable at Vendor's discretion (§ 13.1), a one-month liability cap applying "without exception" (§ 21.1), a one-way unlimited Customer indemnity with no Vendor indemnity at all (§ 20), immediate deletion of Customer Data with no transition assistance (§ 11.1), and a 15-day Deliverable warranty that extinguishes the otherwise open-ended conformance warranty (§ 19.2).

Several of these provisions contradict clauses elsewhere in the same document — § 12.3 records that we have made no exclusivity, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment; §§ 11.2–11.3 provide for data return before deletion; § 13.3 permits revocation only for uncured material breach; § 21.3 defines Excluded Claims that § 21.1 purports to override. The order-of-precedence provision (the second § 2.2) does not resolve internal conflicts within the Agreement. We should treat the inconsistencies as leverage: in each case the Vendor's own drafting already concedes our position elsewhere.

Drafting defects to raise separately: the Agreement contains two provisions numbered § 2.2, and § 9.3 relies on remedies "required by Section 20.5", which does not exist.

---

| 2 | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | High | Compliant | § 24.1 (with §§ 24.2–24.4, 13.3) | Preferred position in full; no Vendor exit or repricing on our change of control. |
| 3 | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | High | Compliant | § 9.4 (with §§ 7.1, 24.4, 27.3) | No Customer-payable LDs, penalties or termination fees anywhere. |
| 4 | T4C — Termination for convenience | High | Compliant | § 9.4 | Preferred position; 30 days' notice, partial termination, refund of prepaid Fees, no Vendor convenience right. |
| 5 | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Medium | Compliant | § 22.1 (with §§ 22.2–22.3) | Preferred position on every material term, including 5% cost-shift trigger and no direct system access. |
| 6 | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Medium | Compliant | § 28.1 (with §§ 28.2–28.3) | New York law, New York County courts; no arbitration provision. |
| 7 | **INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor** | Medium | **Deviation** | § 20 (§ 20.1) | Walk-away: one-way unlimited Customer indemnity, no Vendor indemnity at all; § 9.3 cross-refers to a non-existent § 20.5. |
| 8 | **LICENSE — Licence grant scope** | Medium | **Deviation** | § 13.1 | Walk-away: Customer only, Affiliates and contractors excluded, revocable at Vendor's sole discretion; conflicts with § 13.3. |
| 9 | **LOL-CAP — Liability cap, mutuality, carve-outs** | Medium | **Deviation** | § 21.1 | Walk-away twice over: cap of one month's Fees paid, and "without exception" overrides the § 21.3 Excluded Claims. |
| 10 | MFN — MFN obligations burdening Customer | Medium | Compliant | § 12.3 | No MFN or most-favoured-customer obligation on us; § 12.3 affirmatively confirms this. |
| 11 | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Medium | Compliant | § 12.3 | No non-solicit or no-hire covenant; general recruitment expressly preserved. |
| 12 | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Medium | Compliant | § 8.2 (with § 8.3) | 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, 60-day reminder with deadline extension, CPI/3% uplift cap. |
| 13 | **TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return** | Medium | **Deviation** | § 11.1 | Walk-away: immediate cessation of assistance and permanent deletion, no export; contradicts §§ 11.2–11.3. |
| 14 | **EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer** | Low | **Deviation** | § 2.2 | Walk-away: sole and exclusive supplier for the full three-year term, no category limit, no performance exit; conflicts with § 12.3. |
| 15 | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Low | Compliant | § 18.1 (with § 18.2) | Preferred position on all limits; employer's liability is additional cover in our favour. |
| 16 | **MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments** | Low | **Deviation** | § 2.1 | Walk-away: three-year USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay "without reduction or termination rights"; conflicts with §§ 9.4 and 12.3. |
| 17 | **NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer** | Low | **Deviation** | § 12.4 | Walk-away: 24 months post-term, any competing product, any territory, no internal-development or acquisition carve-out; conflicts with § 12.3. |
| 18 | **WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration** | Low | **Deviation** | § 19.2 | 15-day Deliverable warranty below the fallback and its cut-off extinguishes §§ 19.1 and 19.4 remedies; barely exceeds the § 6.1 acceptance window. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following seven provisions are identified in the findings as walk-away positions under the playbook. They fail both the preferred and the fallback positions on material terms and should be treated as conditions of signature rather than trading chips.

1. **§ 2.1 — Take-or-pay minimum commitment.** Three-year, USD 2,000,000 per year, expressly without reduction or termination rights. Our position: Fees for Services ordered or used only, with no minimum or shortfall obligation. Fallback available in negotiation: a single 12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
2. **§ 2.2 — Sole-source exclusivity.** Full-term exclusivity with no category limit and no exit for service-level or delivery failure. Our position: convert the appointment to non-exclusive, aligning § 2.2 with § 12.3.
3. **§ 12.4 — Post-term non-compete on Customer.** 24 months post-term, any competing product or service, any territory, and it expressly bars acquisitions. Our position: delete. Fallback: named competing product, term only, 12-month cap, with internal-development and acquisition carve-outs.
4. **§ 13.1 — Services licence.** Customer alone, Affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them, revocable at Vendor's sole discretion. Our position: extend to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, tie revocation to the § 13.3 notice-and-cure standard, and permit successor transfer via § 24.
5. **§ 20 — Indemnification.** No Vendor indemnity anywhere in the Agreement, coupled with an unlimited Customer indemnity for "every claim" relating to our use of the Services. Our position: add the Vendor indemnity (IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data incidents, gross negligence and wilful misconduct), narrow our indemnity to Customer-provided content and our breach of law, add notice/control/cooperation procedure and the missing § 20.5 procure/modify/replace/refund remedies.
6. **§ 21.1 — Liability cap.** One month of Fees actually paid, applying "without exception" so that indemnities, confidentiality, data protection and security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement all sit inside a one-month cap. Our position: the greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, delete "without exception" so the § 21.3 Excluded Claims operate uncapped, and keep payment obligations outside the damages exclusion.
7. **§ 11.1 — Post-termination.** Immediate cessation of all assistance and permanent deletion of Customer Data with no export or migration support, directly contradicting §§ 11.2–11.3. Our position: up to six months of transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, with deletion subordinated to §§ 11.2–11.3; 90 days is an acceptable fallback.

**Not walk-away, but must move:** § 19.2. We are seeking a longer Deliverable conformance period and deletion of the correction/refund cut-off, with a non-limitation cross-reference preserving §§ 19.1, 19.3 and the § 6.2 / § 19.4 remedies.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Confirm the redline set before it goes out.** The proposed edits for the exclusivity (§ 2.2), minimum commitment (§ 2.1), non-compete (§ 12.4) and indemnity (§ 20) findings were repaired during verification and should be read once more in context. The proposed edits for the licence (§ 13.1), liability cap (§ 21.1), transition (§ 11.1) and warranty (§ 19.2) findings did not verify and require manual drafting before issue.
2. **Settle the warranty ask internally.** The finding rationale supports extending § 19.2 to 90 days, while the drafted proposal states 12 months for software with 90 days for Services. We should fix a single number before sending the markup.
3. **Use the internal contradictions in the cover note.** For §§ 2.1, 2.2 and 12.4 we can point to Vendor's own acknowledgement in § 12.3 that we have made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment; for § 11.1 to §§ 11.2–11.3; for § 13.1 to § 13.3; and for § 21.1 to § 21.3. Note that the order-of-precedence clause does not resolve conflicts internal to the Agreement, so each must be fixed on its face.
4. **Raise the drafting defects.** Renumber the duplicate § 2.2, and correct or supply the § 20.5 remedies on which § 9.3 depends.
5. **Brief the business owner on the walk-away list.** Items 1–7 above are gating; we should confirm the commercial team's appetite on the take-or-pay and exclusivity items before the first negotiation call, since those two drive the economics of the deal.
6. **Leave the compliant clauses alone.** The IP, assignment, convenience-termination, audit, governing law, renewal, insurance, MFN and non-solicit provisions meet the playbook and, in several cases, favour us. We will not reopen them.
